contexts.text: Given themselves up to idleness and inertia.
In the ultimates of nature, where inert things occur.
Nature in itself is quite inert.
There is not anything so inert and dead that there is nothing of what is efficient in it.

The atmospheres in progressing towards lower things... continually become more compressed and more inert; and at last, in ultimates, so compressed and inert, that they are no longer atmospheres, but substances at rest...
The activity (of the atmospheres) ceases in inertia.
Such appear (there) as if they were mere inertnesses.
Their inertness in thinking about spiritual things, and their consequent inertness in doing any uses. They are called Boreal Spirits.
They pass their time solitary in deserts, as if they were inert...
